stories.title: India-UAE trade nearing pre-war levels, says Piyush Goyal

article_sentences: Trade between India and the UAE will be back to pre-war levels in a few months, Union Minister for Commerce and Industry Piyush Goyal said on Monday.
“Trade between India and the UAE is coming back to pre-war levels.
We are very close to it and in another few months we should get back to normal,” Goyal said after chairing the 14th India-UAE high-level joint task force on investments.
Overall, India’s exports of goods and services rose 15 per cent in the first six months of FY27 despite geopolitical issues, he added.
India and the UAE signed a comprehensive economic partnership agreement in 2022 focusing on bilateral trade and investments.
Last year, bilateral trade between India and the UAE crossed $100 billion, and the two countries plan to double it by 2032.
“Trade has been impacted by the (Iran-US) war and we are looking at ways to restore it and grow it in coming years,” he added.
Goyal said both sides discussed greater cooperation in space technology, shipbuilding, ports, food security, energy and AI.
Political relations between the two countries remain strong, with four meetings between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan over the past two years.
India and the UAE are working together to develop strategic petroleum reserves and liquefied petroleum gas supplies.
A study is also underway to explore construction of undersea gas pipelines from the UAE to India.

The UAE delegation at the task force meeting was led by Minister for Foreign Trade Dr Thani bin Ahmed Al Zeyoudi and Sheikh Hamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, Managing Director of Abu Dhabi Investment Authority.

stories.title: Army chief Dhiraj Seth: Land victory only tangible factor in war

article_sentences: NEW DELHI: Indian Army chief General Dhiraj Seth on Sunday called a land victory the only "tangible factor" of success in a war, despite increasing technological innovations in the defence sector.

In his address at the NDTV Defence Summit 2016, General Seth said: "We see salvo after salvo in today's social media covering warfare across the globe, where information narratives and warfare are being fired to fog the real battle picture, creating uncertainty and confusion...
However, I strongly feel, through all this clutter, one reality that does not change: land will always be the one and only tangible and useful factor of success."
"Victory was, is, and will always be measured in territorial terms and that territory will be occupied, secured, and defended only by the force," he asserted.
"Every capability must address one question: how does it help that soldier who puts his boots or tracks on the ground?
That is why I would place him at the heart of the capability development that you're looking at..."

Recalling a photograph taken on December 16, 1971 that depicted Pakistan surrendering at the end of the Bangladesh Liberation War, the army chief said: "The reason I allude to this today is that photo gave us a very defining moment, because that was the precise moment when the war came to an end.
But there is no demarcating moment; there is no termination point which indicates an end to the hostilities."
He noted that conflict timelines are becoming "increasingly indefinite", with intermittent spikes of intense fighting.
"Technology is certainly shortening the battles, but it is not necessarily shortening the war.
These millennium wars can best be described as wars with pause.
Pause, in fact, is becoming a part of military strategy, with the pause representing not the domination of conflict but merely a change in its intensity and manifestation," General Seth added.

stories.title: 17 tribal habitations under water in Andhra’s Polavaram as Godavari nears first flood warning
stories.summary: Sir Arthur Cotton Barrage takes in 9.66 lakh cusecs on Monday morning, a few thousand short of the 10-lakh warning mark; water officials work Polavaram’s gates to hold the flood below it; 171 villages are on alert

article_sentences: The Godavari valley and delta are bracing for the river’s first flood warning at Dowleswaram.
Upstream in Andhra Pradesh’s Polavaram district, at least 17 tribal habitations are already under water, and 171 villages have been alerted, officials told.
The Hindu.
The Sir Arthur Cotton Barrage took in 9.66 lakh cusecs at 7 a.m. on Monday (September 28, 2026), a little short of the 10-lakh mark at which the warning is issued.
In the 24 hours to Thursday (September 24, 2026) morning, the barrage had received about 83,000 cusecs, according to the Andhra Pradesh Water Resources Information and Management System (APWRIMS).
The Sabari and Sileru rivers are bringing more floodwater into the Godavari, leading to flooding in the Godavari valley and the delta.
Heavy rain in Odisha, Chhattisgarh and Andhra Pradesh, followed by the deep depression last week, is causing a huge inflow into the river.

The APWRIMS’s Godavari basin forecast for September 27 put the peak at the barrage at about 10.1 lakh cusecs on Monday, easing to about 9.8 lakh on Tuesday and 8 lakh on Wednesday (September 30, 2026).
Its officials were working the Polavaram project’s gates to keep the flow at the barrage below the first warning level, the bulletin said.
Upstream, the river was already falling at Kunavaram, Chinturu and Polavaram by Monday afternoon, the river gauges showed.
The Godavari Flood Report-2026 said: “The trend of inflow into the Godavari river at Dowleswaram remains on the rise.
At least 1,400 cusecs of water is being released into the irrigation canals in the Godavari Delta.”

stories.title: Tirupattur TVK MLA’s win by a single vote: Madras High Court rejects election petition filed against his victory
stories.summary: Justice G.K. Ilanthiraiyan allowed an application filed by the MLA R. Seenivasa Sethupathy to reject the election petition preferred by former DMK Minister K.R. Periakaruppan
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Madras High Court on Monday (September 28, 2026) rejected an election petition filed against the victory of Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) MLA R. Seenivasa Sethupathy from Tirupattur constituency in Sivaganga district by a razor-thin margin of just one vote in the 2026 Tamil Nadu Asepolls.

Justice G.K. Ilanthiraiyan allowed an application filed by the TVK MLA to reject the election petition filed by Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) candidate and former Minister K.R. Periakaruppan, who contended that he lost the polls primarily because of the existence of two Legislative Assembly constituencies with the same name ‘Tirupattur’ in Tamil Nadu.
Mr. Sethupathy was declared elected on securing 83,375 votes as against 83,374 votes garnered by Mr. Periakaruppan.

However, the DMK candidate claimed a postal vote belonging to the Tirupattur constituency in Sivaganga district had been inadvertently sent to the Tirupattur constituency in Tirupattur district and that the wrongly transferred vote was not sent back to the right constituency.

Listing out the reasons for seeking a rejection of the election petition, senior counsel V. Raghavachari, assisted by advocates Dixita Gohil and Pranjal Agarwal, argued the election petitioner had presented a “highly implausible” scenario of a postal vote belonging to one constituency having been sent to another constituency just because of their identical names.

He contended the Conduct of Election Rules, 1961, make the identity of the intended constituency extremely difficult to lose by pressing into service multiple independent identifiers, which could enable the authorities to determine the constituency to which a postal ballot belongs.

The counsel pointed out the Tirupattur constituency in Tirupattur district was identified as constituency number 50, whereas the Tirupattur constituency in Sivaganga district was identified as constituency number 185.
He asserted that the constituency number, and not the name, was the key identifier.

He said every voter who intends to exercise his/her franchise through the postal ballot must make an application, using Form 12, to the Returning Officer concerned and therefore, the constituency gets determined emphatically even before the issuance of a postal ballot to an elector.

Further, the postal ballots have the full address of the Returning Officer of the relevant constituency pre-printed, without the need for the voters to fill it up by hand, and the postal covers too clearly mention the constituency name, number, district, and the full address of the Returning Officer.

“This means the postal ballot is not an anonymous page, which can ordinarily be treated as belonging to a constituency which happens to receive it by accident, coincidence, or otherwise,” Mr. Raghavachari said and added that it was the election officials who transport the postal covers.
The senior counsel also argued the election petitioner had not produced any material but for an affidavit filed by Tirupattur district DMK candidate.

stories.headline: G20 powers face divisions over a changing global world order
stories.title: G20 powers face divisions over a changing global world order
stories.summary: United Nations, Sep 28 : Speeches by the world’s leading economies at the UN General Assembly revealed a shared fear that the international order is breaking down, but exposed deep divisions over whether the answer lies in stronger multilateralism, greater national sovereignty or forceful unilateral action. Across five days of debate, the 19 national members of the G20 described a world disrupted by wars, economic coercion, fractured supply chains, technological rivalry and declining trust in international institutions. US President Donald Trump defended military action and an “America First” approach. He criticised international organisations and said the United Nations must “stop imposing the far-left agenda of globalist bureaucrats who nobody ever elected”. China offered a sharply different prescription. Vice President Han Zheng called for the post-war order to be protected and disputes to be resolved through dialogue. “The world wants peace, not war,” Han said. He warned that “protectionism produces no winners” and opposed decoupling and the severing of supply chains. Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov described the emergence of the Global South and East as sovereign centres of power. He accused Western countries of trying to preserve privileges acquired through centuries of dominance. France, Germany, Italy and Britain defended international cooperation but said existing institutions must adapt. French President Emmanuel Macron asked whether countries wanted “a return to the law of the jungle” or “a civilized international society”. German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul called for a UN capable of “resolving conflicts — rather than merely managing them”. Italian Deputy Prime Minister Antonio Tajani said alliances should be seen as bridges rather than walls. British Prime Minister Andy Burnham focused on disinformation, cyberthreats and the risks posed by artificial intelligence. Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva said the UN’s credibility had been damaged by the Security Council’s paralysis. “We all know that there will be no winners on the battlefield. Diplomacy is the only option,” Lula said. Mexico linked peace to inclusive development. Foreign Minister Roberto Velasco Álvarez said: “Peace cannot be decreed or imposed; it is built with social justice.” Argentina offered the strongest rejection of the existing system. President Javier Milei called the UN a “useless organization” that sustained what he described as an arrogant bureaucracy. He argued that international cooperation should not become subordination. India warned that countries far removed from battlefields were paying for wars they did not start. External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar pointed to disruptions in food, fuel, fertiliser, finance and commerce. “Those most impacted often have the least say,” he said. India called for de-escalation, uninterrupted energy and trade flows, and an end to prolonged conflicts. Australia, Canada, Indonesia and South Korea presented middle powers as potential stabilisers between competing blocs. Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said the UN’s mission could not be left solely to great powers, wealthy countries or technology companies. Canadian Foreign Minister Anita Anand said: “We are facing a rupture, not a transition.” She argued that countries could no longer remain overly dependent on any single partner. Indonesia said effective multilateralism must produce visible benefits for families, workers and farmers. “The answer to imperfect multilateralism is not less multilateralism; it is a stronger and better multilateralism,” Foreign Minister Sugiono said. South Korean President Lee Jae Myung called for peaceful coexistence on the Korean Peninsula and renewed dialogue between North Korea and the United States. Japan, meanwhile, stressed resilient Indo-Pacific supply chains, nuclear disarmament and stronger international institutions. South Africa placed inequality at the centre of the debate. It said the richest 10 per cent controlled roughly three-quarters of global wealth while developing countries remained constrained by debt and an unequal climate-finance system. Saudi Arabia linked Gulf stability to global energy security and trade. Türkiye said international law must not be applied differently to powerful and weaker countries. The speeches showed that G20 governments broadly agreed on the symptoms: wars are spreading economic pain, technology is concentrating power and international institutions are losing public confidence. Their proposed remedies, however, ranged from rebuilding multilateral institutions to asserting national control and strategic autonomy. The G20 comprises 19 countries, the European Union and the African Union. Its members account for about 85 per cent of global economic output, more than 75 per cent of international trade and roughly two-thirds of the world’s population. --IANS

stories.summary: The Supreme Court has refused to stay the implementation of UPI Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) from October 15, but has raised key questions over the new charge. The court wants clarity on three crucial issues: who pays, who earns and what is the legal basis for imposing the MDR. The government has maintained that the MDR is a fee and not a tax, while the RBI has explained that the mechanism is similar to MDR charged on debit and credit card transactions. The court has now sought clarity on the amendment and the basis for implementing the charge, with the next hearing scheduled after four weeks. stories.title: SC agrees to examine challenge to acquittal of 22 in Sohrabuddin case
stories.summary: New Delhi, Sep 28 : The Supreme Court on Monday agreed to examine a plea challenging the Bombay High Court's order acquitting 22 accused, including 21 police personnel, in the 2005 alleged fake encounter case involving gangster Sohrabuddin Shaikh, his wife Kausar Bi and his aide Tulsiram Prajapati. A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana issued notice on the plea filed by Nayabuddin Shaikh, brother of Sohrabuddin Shaikh, challenging the May 7 judgment of the Bombay High Court that upheld the acquittal of the accused. stories.headline: India’s BESS Pipeline Set to Hit 45-50 GWh, But 8-9 GWh Faces Delay Risk: Crisil
stories.title: India’s BESS Pipeline Set to Hit 45-50 GWh, But 8-9 GWh Faces Delay Risk: Crisil
stories.summary: India’s rapidly expanding battery energy storage system (BESS) pipeline is facing a potential setback, with around 8-9 GWh of planned capacity at heightened risk of delays due to weak project economics and limited implementation experience among some developers, according to Crisil Ratings. Crisil said nearly 21% of the under-construction BESS capacity, equivalent to about 12 GWh, currently faces weak return potential. The key concern is the rebound in battery prices in 2026, while tariffs for several projects were discovered when battery costs were considerably lower. Developers typically procure batteries around a year after securing project bids, exposing projects awarded in 2025 to the recent increase in battery costs. Additional Execution Risks Of this 12 GWh capacity facing weak return potential, around 8-9 GWh also faces an additional execution risk because of limited implementation experience among project sponsors. Crisil said developers with limited scale or procurement track records could face difficulties in securing batteries and other critical equipment on competitive terms. Higher procurement costs, combined with execution challenges, could further reduce project returns or delay commissioning. The concern comes at a time when India is preparing for a sharp expansion in BESS deployment. Crisil expects 45-50 GWh of BESS capacity to be commissioned during FY2027 and FY2028, compared with only around 1 GWh commissioned by the end of FY2026. However, the rating agency said the 8-9 GWh at higher risk of delay could moderate the overall deployment outlook. Key Pressure Points Battery prices have emerged as a key pressure point for developers. According to Crisil’s analysis, battery prices had fallen consistently until 2025, encouraging developers to bid aggressively on the expectation that the decline would continue. However, prices have since increased. The chart accompanying the report shows stationary-storage battery prices rising from around $50-55/kWh in 2025 to about $70-75/kWh in 2026. At prevailing prices, some projects may struggle to achieve the typical targeted internal rate of return of 12-14%. Crisil estimates that a project with a tariff of around Rs 2.2-2.5 lakh per MW per month and battery prices of $55-65/kWh could generate an IRR of 12-14%. Higher battery costs could therefore make some previously awarded projects financially less attractive. Developers could respond by deferring implementation while waiting for battery prices to become more favourable, Crisil said. This creates a particular risk for projects where tariffs have already been locked in but equipment costs have subsequently risen. Broader BESS Pipeline Despite these challenges, the broader BESS pipeline remains substantial. Around 50-55 GWh of BESS capacity is scheduled for commissioning during FY2027 and FY2028. Around 40 GWh of this has been awarded through government-led auctions, with distribution utilities serving as offtakers, while another 10-15 GWh is expected to cater to commercial and industrial consumers or the merchant market. The sharp increase in storage-linked auctions also indicates growing demand for BESS in India's power system. BESS projects accounted for nearly 40% of total auctioned capacity in FY2026, compared with about 5% in each of FY2024 and FY2025. The growth is being driven partly by the increasing share of renewable energy in India's power mix. Renewable energy accounted for around 39% of installed power generation capacity and around 15% of electricity generation in FY2026, according to Crisil. Since solar generation falls sharply during evening hours when electricity demand typically rises, storage is increasingly required to shift surplus renewable generation to periods of higher demand. However, the sector remains dependent on overseas suppliers for batteries and other critical components. Crisil said geopolitical developments and disruptions in global supply chains therefore remain risks for the BESS pipeline, particularly as most of the awarded capacity is still in development or in the early stages of construction. Overall, Crisil expects the remaining 45-50 GWh of the pipeline to have a higher likelihood of being commissioned during FY2027 and FY2028, pointing to a substantial expansion in India's storage capacity despite near-term pressure from battery prices, project economics and execution capabilities.

stories.title: Blueleaf Energy Acquires 40 MW Operating Wind Asset in Karnataka
stories.summary: Pan-Asian renewable energy platform Blueleaf Energy has acquired a 40 MW operating wind power asset in Karnataka’s Belagavi district. The operational wind farm has eight years of clean energy generation experience and complements Blueleaf Energy’s existing 1.5 GW greenfield portfolio across India. It includes projects under construction and in operation. The company secured its legal, finance, and tax structuring advice from Talwar Thakore & Associates (TT&A) and EY. “This acquisition marks an important milestone as our first operating asset purchase in India. Building upon our established success in greenfield development, we are now pursuing targeted M&A to accelerate our growth and scale our presence while maintaining a strong focus on delivering long-term value for India’s clean energy transition,” said Pratyush Thakur, Country Head, India, Blueleaf Energy. Blueleaf Energy’s Previous Projects in India Previously, Blueleaf Energy, commissioned its 300 MWp Pachora Hybrid Power Project in Madhya Pradesh. The project is jointly owned by Blueleaf Energy and Jakson Green through its parent company, Jakson Limited. The utility-scale wind and solar project has an estimated value of approximately ₹1,900 crore. The merchant project is expected to generate nearly 600 million units (MU) of clean electricity annually, which will be sold on the Indian power market. Blueleaf Energy has also established a presence in Rajasthan through its partnership with Jakson Green, with 280 MWp and 560 MWp ground-mounted solar plants in Bikaner forming part of the 1 GWp Rajasthan Solar Portfolio. The partners recently achieved financial close for the portfolio with Axis Bank, marking the completion of funding for the entirety of the portfolio.

Justice Bagchi observed that by this stage the CBSE had almost entirely covered its ecosystem.
Noting that the policy was notified in March, he suggested a “soft launch” so that Class 6 students could receive the same privilege as Class 7 students, given logistical difficulties.
Senior Advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan, appearing for petitioners, argued that students had complied only because they had no choice.
He pointed out that textbooks were not available online initially and that CBSE deals with about 28.83 lakh students.

stories.summary: The top court underlined that public spaces cannot be allowed to become “zones of high risk” because of “lax patrolling and other preventable administrative deficiencies”
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Monday (September 28, 2026) took suo motu cognisance of a spate of sexual assault incidents against minors and women in Delhi-NCR, seeking a response from the Delhi.

Police and observing that public spaces, including parks, buses and Metro stations, cannot be allowed to become “zones of high risk” because of “lax patrolling and other preventable administrative deficiencies”.

A Bench of Justices J.B. Pardiwala and K. Vinod Chandran took note of several recent cases of sexual violence reported in the national capital, including the alleged rape of a 17-year-old at Astha Kunj park near Lady Shri Ram College, the gang-rape of a minor at Swaroop Nagar, and the sexual assault of another minor inside a bus travelling from Greater Noida to Delhi.

“These incidents, considered alongside recent reports of sexual offences across Delhi-NCR, starkly underline the failure of law enforcement and public administration authorities to guarantee basic public safety.

The right to live with dignity, free from the fear of violence, is an intrinsic facet of the fundamental guarantee of life and personal liberty enshrined under Article 21 of the Constitution,” the Bench said.

The Bench further observed that public spaces, including roads, buses, Metro stations, footbridges and subways, cannot be permitted to become “zones of high risk” because of inadequate illumination, poor surveillance, lax patrolling and other preventable administrative deficiencies.

Expressing serious concern over the alleged gang-rape of a 17-year-old girl in a moving bus that travelled nearly 47 km from Greater Noida to Kashmere Gate in Delhi without being stopped at a single police picket earlier this month, the apex court said it could not help but “draw painful parallels with the 2012 Nirbhaya case”.
The incident, it said, called into question whether systemic law-enforcement mechanisms had made any “meaningful progress” in the decade since then.

While acknowledging that statements by public authorities and elected representatives expressing concern over such incidents were understandable, the Bench said expressions of solidarity, without accountability, failed to address the larger institutional question.
“Expressing solidarity is not a solution to this social evil.

What is required is a measurable response with responsibility and accountability being fixed upon the authorities entrusted with prevention of crime, maintenance of public order and protection of vulnerable persons,” the Bench added.

The court also questioned the police response in the Astha Kunj case, taking note of reports that students of Lady Shri Ram College had previously complained of instances of sexual harassment in the area that had gone unaddressed.

stories.headline: Elavenil Valarivan receives Rs 1.33 crore from Gujarat Dy CM
stories.title: Elavenil Valarivan receives Rs 1.33 crore from Gujarat Dy CM
stories.summary: Gandhinagar, Sep 28 : The Gujarat government has awarded rifle shooter Elavenil Valarivan Rs 1.33 crore under its 'Khel Pratibha Puraskar Yojana' after she won two silver medals at the 2026 Asian Games in Japan, taking the total incentives extended to the athlete by the state to Rs 2.41 crore. Gujarat Deputy Chief Minister Harsh Sanghavi on Monday honoured shooter Elavenil Valarivan for her silver-medal performances in the women’s 10m air rifle team and individual events at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games. Valarivan first helped India win silver in the team event before claiming another silver in the individual competition. She shot 252.4 in the individual final to finish behind Japan’s Taichi Hinata, who won gold with a Games-record score of 253.0. Congratulating Valarivan, Sanghavi said the Gujarat government was committed to providing athletes with the training and facilities required to prepare for international competitions. “An athlete’s international success is the result not only of their own hard work but also of the support and values provided by their parents throughout their journey,” he said. Sanghavi also highlighted Valarivan’s association with the Sanskardham complex, where she studied under the state government’s DLSS scheme, saying her Asian Games performance had brought recognition to Gujarat. “The success of athletes nurtured at Sanskardham could inspire thousands of young athletes across the state,” he added. According to the Gujarat government, Valarivan had previously received Rs 1.33 crore under the Shaktidoot Scheme and Olympic Incentive Scheme, in addition to Rs 74 lakh through schemes including the DLSS Scheme and Khel Mahakumbh. The latest incentive takes the total financial assistance provided to Valarivan by the state government to Rs 2.41 crore. Valarivan, who resides in Ahmedabad’s Maninagar area, has been associated with the state government’s Shaktidoot Scheme since 2017-18 and currently holds an ‘A’ category position under the programme. The 27-year-old has represented India at the 2020 Tokyo Olympics and the 2024 Paris Olympics. She won gold at the ISSF World Cup in Rio de Janeiro in 2019 with a score of 251.7 and received the Arjuna Award from the Central government in 2022. Her international record also includes medals at the Junior World Cups in Suhl and Sydney in 2018, the Asian Airgun Championships and the World University Games in Chengdu, besides podium finishes at international competitions in Munich and Kazakhstan in 2025. Valarivan’s two Asian Games medals came eight years after her continental debut, when a rifle malfunction prevented her from progressing to the final. -- IANS

article_sentences: New Delhi: India's GDP growth in the second quarter of FY2026-27 came in significantly above the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) 7 per cent forecast, prompting expectations of a gradual rate-hiking cycle, according to a HSBC Global Investment Research report.
The report expects the RBI to raise the repo rate by 25 basis points twice in FY27, taking it to 5.75 per cent, as economic growth remains strong and inflationary pressures persist.
"Q2 FY26 GDP growth has come in much higher than the RBI's 7 per cent forecast.
Furthermore, the RBI expects inflation to average more than 5 per cent over the next three quarters.
This combination, we believe, opens the door for gentle rate hikes," the report said.
It also expects the RBI to absorb Rs 5-6 trillion of excess liquidity created by FCNR(B) deposits through durable measures such as open market operation (OMO) sales.
According to the report, inflation is expected to remain close to the RBI's 4 per cent target in the first half of FY27 before rising in the second half.
Headline inflation is projected to average above 5 per cent over the next nine months.
"Brent oil prices have rebounded after briefly falling in June.
El Nino conditions are likely to strengthen in the December quarter, potentially pushing food inflation higher," the report said.
It added that higher input costs could be passed on to consumers by companies, which may push core inflation towards 5 per cent by the end of FY27.
India's GDP growth for the quarter ended June stood at 7.8 per cent.

stories.headline: 1947 promises, not 2019, should Be reference point for J&K: Sajad Lone
stories.title: 1947 promises, not 2019, should Be reference point for J&K: Sajad Lone
stories.summary: Srinagar, Sep 28 : Peoples Conference president and MLA Sajad Lone on Monday said that the commitments made in 1947 should remain the reference point for any discussion on Jammu and Kashmir’s political status and its relationship with India. Speaking in the Jammu and Kashmir Legislative Assembly, as per news agency—Kashmir News Observer(KNO), Lone said he had “full respect” for the Prime Minister and the Supreme Court, but asserted that Jammu and Kashmir’s presence within India was rooted in the commitments made to its people in 1947. “I have full respect for the Prime Minister of India and the Supreme Court of India. But if we are here today, it is not because of any promise made by the Prime Minister or the Supreme Court. We are here because of the promises made to the people of J&K in 1947,” Lone said. He said the original framework envisaged a structure in which the people of Jammu and Kashmir would have a meaningful say in their governance and would enjoy autonomy and powers to take their own decisions. Questioning the constitutional and legal basis of the Centre’s decision to reorganise Jammu and Kashmir as a Union Territory, Lone asked, “Tell me, the Union government that relegated us — is this within the limits of law or not?” Referring to the Supreme Court judgment, Lone said the Court had not answered all questions surrounding whether a state could be converted into a Union Territory in such circumstances. He said the Assembly should not shift its historical reference point while discussing Jammu and Kashmir. “The reference point in this Assembly should be 1947, not 2019. We cannot change the reference point. We cannot change the contours of history,” Lone said. Lone also said political phases and governments would change with time, but the historical commitments made to the people of Jammu and Kashmir should continue to be considered. “This is a phase. How many came and how many went. They will also go one day. You will also go one day. We are also in a phase,” he said. “We should not change the reference point. The reference point has to be 1947,” Lone added.—(KNO)
